title: Displacement reactions
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:57Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Both bank cards teach the same displacement example, but they are written for Year 11 chemistry and explain it through electron loss and ion formation, which is a deeper level than the Year 10 Australian Curriculum point needs, so adapting them would mean changing the depth rather than making small edits.

draft.title: Displacement reactions
card: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal takes the place of a less reactive metal in a compound. The less reactive metal is pushed out and left as a solid element.
Zinc placed in copper sulfate solution becomes coated with copper. Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it forms zinc sulfate and copper is displaced.
If the metal added is less reactive than the metal in the compound, nothing happens. Copper placed in zinc sulfate solution does not react.
A reactivity series ranks metals from most to least reactive. Magnesium is above zinc, and zinc is above copper.
draft.remember: A metal only displaces another metal that is less reactive than itself.

a.q: Which metal could displace copper from copper sulfate solution?
a.why: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it pushes copper out of the compound. Silver is less reactive than copper, so it cannot displace it.
a.clue: The metal added must be more reactive than copper.

b.q: Tariq puts a clean zinc strip into magnesium sulfate solution. Magnesium is more reactive than zinc. What is the result?
opts: No reaction, because zinc is less reactive than magnesium
Zinc is coated with magnesium, because it is a metal
Zinc dissolves and magnesium forms, as zinc is more reactive
The solution reacts, because all metals displace each other
b.why: Zinc is less reactive than magnesium, so it cannot push magnesium out of its compound. Both are metals, but reactivity decides the outcome, not just being a metal.
b.clue: Compare the reactivity of the metal added with the metal in solution.

b.best: No reaction, because zinc is less reactive than magnesium
